### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A04 appears in about 60% of traces (up from about 19%), and its mean position shifts from about 0.54 to 0.21, i.e. it occurs earlier in the trace. [OCC001, POS001]
- Activity A27 appears in about 52% of traces, down from 100%. [OCC003]
- Activities A32, A33 and A38 are absent in the earlier window and appear in about 50%, 49% and 49% of traces in the later window, respectively. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- Activity A06 appears in about 4% of traces, down from about 20%. [OCC002]
- The outgoing behaviour of A14 changes: in the earlier window about 87% of its transitions go to A15; in the later window about 54% go to A04 and about 44% go to A15. [DIR004]
- The outgoing behaviour of A26 changes: in the earlier window about 95% of its transitions go to A27; in the later window about 51% go to A27, about 18% to A33, about 17% to A38 and about 15% to A32. [DIR006]
- A04's outgoing behaviour becomes concentrated on A15 (about 87% in the later window, versus a spread over many targets before). [DIR001]
- A32, A33 and A38, which had no outgoing transitions before, now lead mainly to A28 and to each other. [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009]
- The co-occurrence of A14 with A04 rises from about 19% to 60%, with A14 before A04 in about 56% of traces. [REL001]
- The co-occurrence of A14 with A15 rises from about 19% to 60%, with A04 before A15 in about 31% and interleaved in about 27% of traces. [REL002]
- The co-occurrence of A26 with A27 falls from 100% to about 52%, with A26 occurring alone in about 49% of traces. [REL017]
- The co-occurrence of A26 with A32 rises from 0% to 50%, with A26 before A32 in 50% of traces. [REL018]
- The co-occurrence of A27 with A28 falls from 100% to about 52%, with A28 occurring alone in about 49% of traces. [REL021]
- The co-occurrence of A28 with A32 rises from 0% to 50%, with A32 before A28 in about 49% of traces. [REL025]
- The lag between A14 and A04 becomes mostly 1 step (about 96% in the later window, up from about 57%). [LAG001]
- The lag between A14 and A15 shifts: 1-step drops from about 46% to 24%, while 2-step rises from about 8% to 31%. [LAG002]
- The lag between A26 and A28 shifts: 2-step drops from about 91% to 50%, while 4-step rises from 0% to 46%. [LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that a new alternative path is introduced in the later window: A14 now often goes to A04 before continuing to A15, and A26 now often goes to A32/A33/A38 before continuing to A28, while the previous direct A14→A15 and A26→A27→A28 paths still occur in about half of the cases. A27 becomes optional (present in about half of traces), and A04, A32, A33 and A38 appear as new activities. This is directly shown by the changes in outgoing transitions (DIR004, DIR006, DIR001), co-occurrence and order (REL001, REL002, REL017, REL018, REL021, REL025), and lag distributions (LAG001, LAG002, LAG003), together with the occurrence and position changes (OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, POS001). The screening count (55 items vs. 0.73 expected by chance) makes it very unlikely that these differences are random sampling noise.

A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that the new activities A32, A33 and A38 are not a single ordered block: their mutual order is mixed (both orders appear in similar proportions), so the exact internal sequence among them is not fixed. Also, the decrease of A06 (OCC002) is not clearly connected to this main path and may reflect a separate change.

Other differences: A06 participation drops from about 20% to 4% [OCC002].
